Came here twice during recent trip to HCMC and both times were great! The selection of draft craft beers is fantastic, and they also have lots of other good food and drink options. 

The first time we tried a "beer flight" - a selection of six taster-size glasses so you can decide which ones you like best. We particularly enjoyed the Pomelo IPA and Jasmine IPA. The Blonde was very good too. Once you've decided which you like best you can order a small, medium or large (pint) size glass.

We also tried some of the snacks, the tuna tataki was very good, and one of the gins - everything was excellent. 

The staff are really knowledgeable about the beers and which to recommend, and the service was both efficient and friendly. Definitely a place to try if you're in HCMC!

Tasty beer and food!

I did not expect to find ‘real’ craft beer in Vietnam. I am so pleasantly surprised. I got a flight; I had the Irish Stout, Jasmine Red, Session IPA, Pomello IPA, Double Jasmine IPA, and the special Stout (I forget the exact name; it’s an extra charge) It was super delicious! Cherry and chocolate notes. Yum! 
I had the Pasteur Street hamburger which comes with fries. It was delicious. My wife had the Omelette with crab and rice and it was delicious as well. It was also delicious. We had the fried ground duck with rice crackers and the onion rings for an appetizer. I recommend both. 
The service was impeccabile. Our waiter was very friendly and helped us order food. Everything is in English so there was no problem ordering. My wife does not like spicy foods, so the waiter made sure nothing was spicy, and brought me some Tabasco to spice up my food. 
I HIGHLY recommend eating here if you’re in the area. There is a bit of variety in the menu, so you’re not limited to one or two choices.

Found this place on the second day of our trip to Saigon, and went back every day for the remaining three days of our visit. Mainly drank the Jasmine (West Coast style) IPA while we were there, reserving the 13% Russian Imperial Stout and 9.2% DIPA as "ones for the road".
